sentences.text:
Shri G.P. Patel - Advocate for the appellan
 Shri Ashish Kurmi - Panel Lawyer for the re
Heard on admission.
Heard on I.A. No.1112/2023, which is first application filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

The appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 450, 376(1) of I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.2000/- and R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.
3000/- respectively with default stipulations.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting the appellant for aforesaid offence.
As per the case of the prosecution, the prosecutrix was major at the time of incident.
It is a case of consent.
The Doctor opined that penetrative intercourse is not possible as hymen was found intact.
There was no internal or external injury found on the person of the prosecutrix.

The appellant is in custody and there is a bleak possibility of disposal of this appeal in near future, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
Panel Lawyer has opposed the application.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and statement of the prosecutrix, I find it to be a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail,
therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, this application is allowed.
Sonu Dhanakk vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50717504/
1 I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant Sonu Dhanakk shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court concerned on 21.08.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
